This changes a saved preference, not the connection (no OAuth needed); the current value shows in GetMcpServerStatus when it's been customized.

server_id.description: The server identifier shown by GetMcpServerStatus. It is the same identifier that GetDynamicTools and CallDynamicTool address, e.g. "dashboard-team-1-Slack". Never a display name.

instructions.description: The custom instructions to follow whenever you use this connector. They say how the user wants it used (e.g. "Reply in threads on Slack."). Pass an empty string to clear them and fall back to the connector's default.

StopSubagent.name: StopSubagent
StopSubagent.description: Abort background subagents you dispatched (via Task). Pass one subagent's id as subagent_id (the "Agent ID:" line of the Task result) to kill a subagent that is wedged, looping with no progress, or no longer needed, for example a computerUse subagent stuck on the box desktop. Pass all: true instead to stop everything at once: every running subagent, plus, where this host can reach them, the other agents you handed work to (peers you messaged with priority and cloud agents you launched); the result says when it could not reach them. This is the call to make when the user asks you to stop, halt, cancel, or quit the current work, and it must be your first action for that request rather than checking or stopping children one by one. Stopping tears the subagent down and frees its box desktop window; it does not come back, and you are not separately revived for it (this tool's result is the confirmation, and with all: true it lists exactly which ids were stopped, which had already finished, which could not be stopped, and what happened to each peer and cloud agent). If you instead want a subagent to change course and keep going, use MessageSubagent.

subagent_id.description: One running subagent's id, from the "Agent ID:" line of the Task result that dispatched it. Omit it when all is true.

all.description: Set true to abort every background subagent you have running, in one call, instead of naming one, and with them, where this host can reach them, every other agent you handed work to: peers you messaged with priority and cloud agents you launched (the result says when it could not). Use this whenever the user asks you to stop, halt, cancel, or quit the current work: it stops each running child independently (computerUse, executor, and any other Task children, plus anything those children started), delivers a stop to each peer (which then stops its own subagents the same way), cancels each running cloud agent, and the result lists exactly which ids were stopped, which had already finished, and which could not be stopped and why. Do not combine with subagent_id.

Task.name: Task
Task.description:
Start a subagent: a separate agent that works on one task and reports back to you.
- It cannot see this conversation or the user. Its prompt must be self-contained: the goal, the context and exact values it needs, and what to report back.
- To follow up with an agent that finished, pass its ID as resume; it keeps its context. Without resume, each call starts fresh.
- Its final message comes back to you, not the user. Trust it.

Available subagent_types and descriptions are listed in <available_subagent_types> in the initial user-info message at the start of this conversation.

When an agent runs in the background, you will be automatically notified when it completes after you end your own turn - do NOT AwaitShell or poll it. Continue with other work or end your turn instead. Don't mention this to the user.

description.description: A short, user-friendly title for the subagent. This appears in the UI as the subagent's name. Make it concrete and distinct, consider recent titles to avoid reuse. For resumed subagents which you are prompting to work on a separate task, give an updated description based on the latest work the subagent is performing. (Do not rename if the subagent is continuing work on the same high-level task.)

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

resume.description: Optional agent ID to resume from. If provided, sends a follow-up message to the agent after it has completed. Requests to a currently running asynchronous agent fail; wait for completion before resuming.

subagent_type.description: Subagent type to use for this task. Must be one of: executor, videoReview, watchVideo, computerUse.

file_attachments.description: Optional array of file paths to images or videos to attach to the subagent. Files are read and attached to the subagent's context. Use to forward relevant media to any subagent (e.g. pass a user-attached image's saved file path so the subagent sees the actual image rather than a prose description).

run_in_background.description: Run the agent in the background (returns output_file path to check later). If this is false, you will be blocked until the agent completes. When true, the background subagent will send a notification when it completes.

TodoWrite.name: TodoWrite
TodoWrite.description:
Your task queue: the durable list of everything the user has asked for, across all your parallel streams of work.

When to use:
- The moment a request arrives, record it as a todo before dispatching or starting it.
- Update statuses in real time: in_progress when its work starts, completed the moment its result is delivered to the user, cancelled when the user drops it or changes their mind.
- On every wake (a user message or a finished background task), reconcile the list first: what's running, what landed, what to dispatch next.

States and parallelism:
- pending: not yet started. in_progress: actively being worked, by you or a background worker. completed: result delivered to the user. cancelled: no longer needed.
- SEVERAL todos are normally in_progress at once, one per independent stream running in parallel (each dispatched worker, plus at most one thing you are doing inline). Never serialize independent streams just to keep a single one in_progress.
- Keep the list current rather than perfect: cancel stale items instead of leaving them pending, and prune long-finished ones when the list gets noisy.

Skip it for purely conversational replies and trivial one-step lookups you answer inline immediately.

id.description: Unique identifier for the TODO item

content.description: The description/content of the todo item

status.description: The current status of the TODO item

todos.description: Array of TODO items to update or create

merge.description: Whether to merge the todos with the existing todos. If true, the todos will be merged into the existing todos based on the id field. You can leave unchanged properties undefined. If false, the new todos will replace the existing todos.

UninstallMcpServer.name: UninstallMcpServer
UninstallMcpServer.description: Remove ONE custom MCP server by its server identifier. A custom server is one added with AddMcpServer, not one that came from a plugin. This is destructive and deletes the server with all of its accounts, which signs the user out of it, so confirm with the user via a question widget first. Only remove a server the user asked to remove, never to fix one. To fix a connector that is failing or needs sign-in, reconnect it with RestartMcpServers or sign in again with AuthenticateMcpServer, and otherwise tell the user what failed. A server the listing marks `plugin=<id>` came from a marketplace plugin. Removing it would uninstall that WHOLE plugin, which this tool refuses. Use UninstallPlugin for those so the confirmation can disclose the full scope. To remove just one account and keep the server, use RemoveMcpAccount instead.

server_id.description: The server identifier shown by GetMcpServerStatus. It is the same identifier that GetDynamicTools and CallDynamicTool address, e.g. "dashboard-team-1-Slack". Never a display name.

UninstallPlugin.name: UninstallPlugin
UninstallPlugin.description: Uninstall a plugin by its STABLE plugin id (from SearchPlugins). This is destructive and removes the WHOLE PLUGIN, meaning its install record and EVERY connector and skill it added, so confirm with the user via a question widget first, and your confirmation must disclose that full scope (list what goes). It also signs the user out of every connector it added, and installing it again does not bring a sign-in back. Only uninstall a plugin the user asked to remove, never to fix or reinstall one of its connectors. To fix a connector that is failing or needs sign-in, reconnect it with RestartMcpServers or sign in again with AuthenticateMcpServer, and otherwise tell the user what failed. Plugins required by the user's team cannot be uninstalled. This removes each of its servers with ALL of their accounts; to remove just one account from a server, use RemoveMcpAccount instead.

plugin_id.description: The stable plugin id from SearchPlugins.

UpdateAgent.name: UpdateAgent
UpdateAgent.description: Edit an existing agent's profile: its name and/or description. Only the fields you provide are changed; the rest are left exactly as they were, and there is no way to clear or delete an agent through this tool. Use it to refine a teammate you (or the user) created.

agent_id.description: The id of the agent to update.

name.description: A new name for the agent. Omit to leave the name unchanged.

description.description: A new persona/description for the agent. Omit to leave it unchanged.

UpdateChannel.name: UpdateChannel
UpdateChannel.description: Add and/or remove member agents of an existing channel (a group chat) by its id. Only the ids you pass change; the rest of the roster stays exactly as it was, and a channel holds at most 6 members. A channel always keeps at least one member. A removal that would empty it is refused. Members you add see the channel in their next channel turn; removed members simply stop receiving its posts. You can only change channels you are currently a member of; any other channel is reported as not found.

channel_id.description: The id of the channel to change.

add_member_ids.description: Agent ids to add to the channel. Ids that are not existing agents are ignored.

remove_member_ids.description: Agent ids to remove from the channel.

UpdateSkill.name: UpdateSkill
UpdateSkill.description: Save, rewrite, or delete one of your reusable skills. A skill has no trigger; a saved task that runs on a schedule is a routine. Cursor-managed skills can't be changed.

id.description: An existing skill's id. Required for delete. On write, pass it only to rewrite that skill; omit it to create one (its id is made from the name).

description.description: Required on write: one line a reader uses to decide it applies ("use this when …").

body.description: Required on write. The recipe, in markdown.

UpdateProfile.name: UpdateProfile
UpdateProfile.description: Change your profile and settings. Only the fields you pass change. For your picture use UpdateAvatar.

name.description: Your name, the chat title the user sees.

title.description: Short role label beside your name ("Designer"); "" clears it.

avatar_shape.description: Your default mark, hidden while a custom picture is installed.

hidden_from_sidebar.description: Hides your sidebar row; you stay reachable through Cmd-K and Hidden chats.

notify_on_updates.description: The "Notify me about this assistant" toggle.

drafting_disabled.description: Pass false to turn draft cards back on when the user asks. You can't turn them off; tell the user to click "Disable drafts for this Bot" on a draft card. Owner only.

UpdateAvatar.name: UpdateAvatar
UpdateAvatar.description: Set or clear your profile picture. Write or download the image first.

path.description: set only. Absolute path to a png/jpg/webp/gif/svg under 5 MB, on your box (under /workspace is fine) or the user's computer.

DisconnectChannel.name: DisconnectChannel
DisconnectChannel.description: Disconnect one of your channels; the live connection closes within seconds.

WebFetch.name: WebFetch
WebFetch.description:
Fetch content from a specified URL and return its contents in a readable markdown format. Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze webpage content.

- The URL must be a fully-formed, valid URL.
- This tool is read-only and will not work for requests intended to have side effects.
- This fetch tries to return live results but may return previously cached content.
- Authentication is not supported, and an error will be returned if the URL requires authentication.
- If the URL is returning a non-200 status code, e.g. 404, the tool will not return the content and will instead return an error message.
- This fetch runs from an isolated server. Hosts like localhost or private IPs will not work.
- This tool does not support fetching binary content, e.g. media or PDFs.
- For static assets and non-webpage URLs, use the `Shell` tool instead.


Some sites' firewalls block this tool's fetch provider with a 403 or a block page (e.g. "Request Rejected"). That is not evidence the page does not exist: fall back to a browser subagent when one is available, or `curl` via Shell (your box egresses from a different network).

url.description: The URL to fetch. The content will be converted to a readable markdown format.

WebSearch.name: WebSearch
WebSearch.description:
Search the web for real-time information about any topic. Returns summarized information from search results and relevant URLs.

Use this tool when you need up-to-date information that might not be available or correct in your training data, or when you need to verify current facts.
This includes queries about:
- Libraries, frameworks, and tools whose APIs, best practices, or usage instructions are frequently updated. ("How do I run Postgres in a container?")
- Current events or technology news. ("Which AI model is best for coding?")
- Informational queries similar to what you might Google ("kubernetes operator for mysql")

IMPORTANT - Use the correct year in search queries:
- Today's date is 2026-10-19. You MUST use this year when searching for recent information, documentation, or current events.
- Example: If today is 2026-10-19 and the user asks for "latest React docs", search for "React documentation 2026", NOT "React documentation 2025"

Results come from an external search index that some sites block, so a missing or stale result is not evidence a page or fact does not exist. When search comes up empty for something that should exist, try WebFetch on a likely URL, then fall back to a browser subagent when one is available, or `curl` via Shell.

search_term.description: The search term to look up on the web. Be specific and include relevant keywords for better results. For technical queries, include version numbers or dates if relevant.

explanation.description: One sentence explanation as to why this tool is being used, and how it contributes to the goal.

FindContacts.name: FindContacts
FindContacts.description: Look up people by name in the user's Contacts on their Mac. Each match carries `name`, `phones` in E.164 (pass one straight to FindIMessageChats `handle` or SendIMessage `to`), and `emails`. `region` is the Mac's country: a number stored without a country code was read as that country's. `unresolvedPhones` are numbers as the user stored them that could not be read as complete; quote them and ask rather than guessing. `total` counts every match. A person never messaged from this Mac has no chat; that is not a reason to stop, send to the phone.

query.description: A person's name or the start of one; matches any name part, case-insensitively.

FindIMessageChats.name: FindIMessageChats
FindIMessageChats.description: Find chats in the user's Messages app on their Mac, by group title or by participant handle (E.164 phone or email). Returns each chat's `guid` (the chat id the other Messages tools take; `identifier` is not it), participants, service, and last activity, most recently active first, with `total` counting every match. Start here. `people` maps the handles in the result that matched a Contacts entry to that person's name; call people by that name, and show a handle only when it has no entry.

displayName.description: Match a group chat by its exact title, not a substring. One-to-one chats have no title, so this never finds a person; get the handle from FindContacts.

handle.description: Match a chat whose participant handle equals this exactly, as Messages stores it: an E.164 number (`+15555550100`) or an email.

limit.description: Max results to return; the newest are kept. Defaults to 50; the Mac clamps to 500.

ChatItems.name: ChatItems
ChatItems.description: Read a Messages conversation on the user's Mac: messages with their reply threading, tapbacks, edits, unsends, attachments, and group events, newest last. Returns the newest page; `total` counts every item, and a truncated result carries `nextBefore` to pass as `before` for the next-older page. On a message, `handle` is the other party (the recipient on the user's own one-to-one messages, absent on their group messages), never the user's own address, and `body.fallback: true` means the text was recovered lossily. `people` maps the handles in the result that matched a Contacts entry to that person's name; call people by that name, and show a handle only when it has no entry.

chatGuid.description: The chat's guid, from FindIMessageChats (e.g. `iMessage;-;+15555550100`). Omitting it reads the whole history, keeps only the newest page, and truncates; prefer a guid, SearchIMessages, or IMessageActivity.

limit.description: Max results to return; the newest are kept. Defaults to 50; the Mac clamps to 200.

before.description: Copy a truncated result's `nextBefore` (`{date, id}`) verbatim to get the next-older page.

SearchIMessages.name: SearchIMessages
SearchIMessages.description: Search the user's Messages history on their Mac across every chat. Matches are case-insensitive substrings of message bodies only, not attachments, group titles, names, or handles. Returns the newest matches with their chat guids, so you can follow one up with ChatItems; `total` counts every match, and a truncated result carries `nextBefore` to pass as `before` for the next-older page. `people` maps the handles in the result that matched a Contacts entry to that person's name; call people by that name, and show a handle only when it has no entry.

query.description: Text to look for in message bodies.

limit.description: Max results to return; the newest are kept. Defaults to 25; the Mac clamps to 100.

before.description: Copy a truncated result's `nextBefore` (`{date, id}`) verbatim to get the next-older page.

IMessageActivity.name: IMessageActivity
IMessageActivity.description: Count messages sent and received per chat over a time window in the user's Messages history, as `{chatGuid, count, handles, displayName}` rows, most recently active chat first; `chatGuid` is what ChatItems takes. `people` maps the handles in the result that matched a Contacts entry to that person's name; call people by that name, and show a handle only when it has no entry. Use this to see which chats have been active before reading any conversation.

since.description: Start of the window (inclusive), an ISO-8601 timestamp with offset.

until.description: End of the window (exclusive), an ISO-8601 timestamp with offset. Omit to run up to now.

FetchIMessageAttachment.name: FetchIMessageAttachment
FetchIMessageAttachment.description: Fetch one attachment from a message in the user's Messages history. Images come back inline for you to look at (HEIC arrives as JPEG); anything else lands on your box at a path you then open with Read. Fails for attachments over 100 MiB or not yet downloaded to the Mac; tell the user rather than retrying.

messageGuid.description: The guid of the message carrying the attachment.

attachmentGuid.description: The attachment's guid, from the message's `attachments` list.

SendIMessage.name: SendIMessage
SendIMessage.description: Send a message from the user's Mac, as the user. Address it with exactly one of `to` (one handle) or `chatId` (a chat guid); a call with both is rejected. Every call raises an approval card the user must accept, unless the user has allowed that recipient, or every send, on their computer; send once and report the result. `via` echoes how it was addressed, and `verified` is whether the text has already appeared in the local chat log, so `false` means not seen yet, not failed. Never resend on `verified: false`.

to.description: One recipient's handle, exactly an E.164 number (`+15555550100`) or an email; a name or a national-format number is rejected before anything is sent. Get a number from FindContacts. Reaches a one-to-one chat only. Use this or `chatId`.

chatId.description: The chat's `guid` from FindIMessageChats (`iMessage;+;chat…` for a group), not its `identifier`. The only way to reach a group chat. Use this or `to`.

service.description: `iMessage` or `SMS` to force one. Omit (or `auto`) to try iMessage, then SMS only if the address is not on iMessage. Ignored with `chatId`, whose guid already carries the service.

recipientName.description: The recipient's name exactly as FindContacts returned it. Only a `to` send shows it, on the approval card beside the handle; a `chatId` card shows a one-to-one chat's handle or "Group chat", never a name. So to text one person whose handle and name you have, send with `to` and this, even if you found their chat. Omit when you do not have one.

CheckIMessagePermissions.name: CheckIMessagePermissions
CheckIMessagePermissions.description: Report which grants the user's Mac has given the Messages tools: `fullDiskAccess` (reading history), `automation` (sending; `notAsked` can also mean Messages.app is not running), and `contacts` (FindContacts). Call it when a Messages tool fails with a denied or `helper_…_failed` error, then tell the user which grant to give. A declined approval card is not a permission problem.

ListCredentials.name: ListCredentials
ListCredentials.description: Search connected 1Password logins by website/domain or service name. Returns titles and sites, never credential values. Matching saved logins fill automatically in the live browser. If several match, choose the appropriate login from the task context; ask only when the choice cannot be determined. Use secure forms when no saved login is available.

site.description: Current website URL or domain. Always pass this when a browser login is blocked; only credentials allowed for that live site are returned.

query.description: Optional service/name search when no website URL is available, e.g. reform or stripe.

GetCredentialProviderStatus.name: GetCredentialProviderStatus
GetCredentialProviderStatus.description: Read the user's current saved-credential provider status from Cursor's backend. Call this when the user asks whether their password manager, vault, saved credentials, or 1Password connection is connected, how many saved items exist, or whether renewal needs attention. Never infer status from chat history or the filesystem. The tool returns only provider-neutral counts and health metadata, never secret values, item titles or sites, provider item IDs, vault IDs, tokens, or fill authority.

UploadFile.name: UploadFile
UploadFile.description:
Send a file from your computer to one of the user's connected services using the account they already connected. The file's bytes go straight from your computer to the service: you never read or paste them, so this works for any size or type up to the limit, and it is the right tool whenever the user wants a file you made or downloaded to land in one of these services. Do not read a file and re-create it with that service's own tools; upload it. The result names the created item and, where the service provides one, a link you can hand to the user.
connection is the connection's identifier: the same one GetMcpServerStatus lists and that connection's own tools are prefixed with (for example user-onedrive, dashboard-team-1-Google-drive, user-SharePoint-xai or user-Gmail--personal). The service short name (google-drive, onedrive, sharepoint, gmail or outlook) is accepted when exactly one account of that service is connected; with several accounts, name the identifier so the right account is used. Supported today:
- Google Drive: destination.path is a folder path from My Drive root (e.g. "Reports/2026"; the folders must already exist), or destination.folderId is a Drive folder id from the Drive listing tools. Omit both for My Drive root. A new file is always created; Drive allows several files with one name. destination.convertToGoogleFormat, when true, asks Drive to import a convertible Office or text file as native Docs, Sheets, or Slides on that same create (pptx → Slides, docx → Docs, xlsx → Sheets). Types Drive cannot import stay as the original file. The result mimeType tells you which landed. Default false.
- OneDrive: destination.path is a folder path from the OneDrive root (e.g. "Documents/Reports"; the folders must already exist), or destination.folderId is a folder item id from list_drive_items. Omit both for the root. An existing file with the same name fails the upload unless destination.overwrite is true.
- Gmail: destination.draftId is the id create_draft returned (or one from list_drafts); the file is attached and the id stays the same, so then send that draftId with send_draft (send_message on Google's hosted Gmail). Attach last: Gmail's update_draft removes every attachment it is not handed again, so finish recipients, subject and body before calling UploadFile, and never call update_draft on a draft that already has an attachment (make a new draft and attach again instead). The draft with its attachments must stay under 25 MB.
- Outlook: on the Outlook connection, destination.draftId is the id create_draft returned; then send_draft it. send_mail cannot carry this file. A Gmail or Outlook draft here carries a file; it is not how you draft for review.
- SharePoint: destination.folderId is the drive id from sharepoint_list_drives and is required. destination.path is the folder under that drive (for example "Reports/2026") and is passed together with folderId; omit path to use the drive root. An existing file with the same name fails unless destination.overwrite is true.
destination.name sets the file name; it defaults to the source file's name. Never put a file's contents into a mail tool's attachments argument yourself; that path cannot carry a real file. A connection that cannot receive files answers with the ones that can.

sourcePath.description: Absolute path of the file on your computer, e.g. the path a Shell command or CopyToBox produced. Only files under /workspace or your own agent directory (/home/box/agent-data/agents/<your id>) can be sent; directories are not accepted.

path.description: Folder path inside the destination service, e.g. "Reports/2026". Omit to use the service root. For SharePoint this is the folder under the drive named by folderId.

folderId.description: Provider folder id, when you already have one from that connection's listing tools. Google Drive and OneDrive take at most one of path or folderId. SharePoint needs folderId (the drive id) and takes path alongside it.

draftId.description: Gmail and Outlook only: the id of an unsent draft to attach the file to. Not combined with path or folderId.

name.description: File name at the destination. Defaults to the source file's name.

overwrite.description: OneDrive and SharePoint only: replace a file that already exists at the destination. Default false: an existing file makes the upload fail so you can pick another name.

convertToGoogleFormat.description: Google Drive only: if the file has a Google Workspace equivalent, upload it as that native type on this create (pptx/ppt/odp → Slides, docx/doc/odt/rtf/html/md/txt → Docs, xlsx/xls/ods/csv/tsv → Sheets). Types Drive cannot import stay as the original file. Default false. Other connections ignore this.

destination.description: Where the file lands; which fields apply depends on the connection.

DownloadFile.name: DownloadFile
DownloadFile.description:
Fetch a file from one of the user's connected services onto your computer using the account they already connected. The file's bytes go straight from the service to your computer: you never read or paste them, so this works for any size or type up to the limit, and it is the right tool whenever you need to work on a file that lives in one of these services (read it, convert it, attach it, upload it somewhere else). Do not ask a service's own tools to print a file's contents into the conversation; download it and open it locally. The result tells you where the file landed.
connection is the connection's identifier: the same one GetMcpServerStatus lists and that connection's own tools are prefixed with (for example user-onedrive, dashboard-team-1-Google-drive, user-SharePoint-xai or user-Gmail--personal). The service short name (google-drive, onedrive, sharepoint, gmail or outlook) is accepted when exactly one account of that service is connected; with several accounts, name the identifier so the right account is used. Supported today:
- Google Drive: source.fileId is a Drive file id from the Drive listing or search tools. Google Docs, Sheets, Slides and Drawings have no file of their own and are exported as .docx, .xlsx, .pptx and .png; the returned name carries that extension.
- OneDrive: source.fileId is an item id from list_drive_items or search_drive_items, or source.path is a path from the OneDrive root (e.g. "Documents/notes.txt").
- Gmail: source.fileId is "<message id>/<attachment id>", both from get_thread or read_email (each attachment listed on a message carries an id). This is the only way to get an email attachment's bytes; the Gmail tools themselves never return them.
- Outlook: source.fileId is "<message id>/<attachment id>", both from get_mail_message (each attachment it lists carries an id). This is the only way to get an Outlook attachment's bytes; the Outlook tools themselves never return them.
- SharePoint: source.fileId is "{drive_id}/{item_id}" from sharepoint_ls or sharepoint_search_documents. A path is not accepted.
destination.path is the full path on your computer, name included; omit it to land the file in your downloads folder under the service's file name. A connection that cannot serve files answers with the ones that can.

fileId.description: Provider file id from that connection's listing or search tools. Google Drive takes ids only.

path.description: OneDrive only: file path from the OneDrive root, e.g. "Documents/notes.txt". Provide exactly one of fileId or path.

source.description: Which file to pull. Provide exactly one of fileId or path.

path.description: Absolute path on your computer for the file, name included; only paths under /workspace or your own agent directory (/home/box/agent-data/agents/<your id>) are accepted. Omit to land it in your downloads folder under the service's file name; the result tells you where. An existing file at the path is replaced.

destination.description: Where the file lands on your computer.

RequestCookieOriginApproval.name: RequestCookieOriginApproval
RequestCookieOriginApproval.description: List Chrome cookie origins on the user's computer, or ask the user to approve importing cookies for one or more origins. Omit origins to list. Pass origins to open the approval dialog and wait for Approve once, Always allow, or Deny. Already-granted pairs are skipped. Do not invent origins. Listing origins (omitting origins) is always fine. Do not request origins for Linear, Okta, United Airlines (united.com), Rippling, Databricks, or Airtable unless the listing shows the user's Chrome has the site: for those, a login made fresh just to feed the import does not persist, so with no existing Chrome session send the user to the normal sign-in on the box instead.

profileId.description: Chrome profile directory id exactly as listed, e.g. "Default" or "Profile 2". Never the user-visible display name: "Work" or "Person 1" are display names, not profile ids.

origins.description: Chrome cookie hosts to request. Omit or pass [] to list available profile and origin pairs. A bare host asks across every profile that has it; pass { origin, profileId } to ask for one profile only. Pass one or more entries to open the approval dialog and wait.

browser_navigate.name: browser_navigate
browser_navigate.description: Fallback only: use for a step that failed in two browser_run_code scripts or hit policy_denied. Navigate to a URL. The result arrives once the page has loaded; no wait is needed.

browser_snapshot.name: browser_snapshot
browser_snapshot.description: Capture the current page's accessibility tree with refs for actions; better than a screenshot. Action results already report the URL and title, so snapshot only when you need a ref you don't have.

target.description: The ref from the latest snapshot or browser_find (never text= or :has-text())

depth.description: Limit the depth of the snapshot tree

browser_click.name: browser_click
browser_click.description: Fallback only: use for a step that failed in two browser_run_code scripts or hit policy_denied. Perform click on a web page

element.description: Short plain-language name of the element, shown to the user in review

target.description: The ref from the latest snapshot or browser_find (never text= or :has-text())

doubleClick.description: Whether to perform a double click instead of a single click

button.description: Button to click, defaults to left

browser_type.name: browser_type
browser_type.description: Fallback only: use for a step that failed in two browser_run_code scripts or hit policy_denied. Type text into editable element

element.description: Short plain-language name of the element, shown to the user in review

target.description: The ref from the latest snapshot or browser_find (never text= or :has-text())

text.description: Text to type into the element

submit.description: Whether to submit entered text (press Enter after)

slowly.description: Whether to type one character at a time. Useful for triggering key handlers in the page. By default entire text is filled in at once.

browser_select_option.name: browser_select_option
browser_select_option.description: Fallback only: use for a step that failed in two browser_run_code scripts or hit policy_denied. Select an option in a dropdown

element.description: Short plain-language name of the element, shown to the user in review

target.description: The ref from the latest snapshot or browser_find (never text= or :has-text())

values.description: Array of values to select in the dropdown. This can be a single value or multiple values.

browser_press_key.name: browser_press_key
browser_press_key.description: Fallback only: use for a step that failed in two browser_run_code scripts or hit policy_denied. Press a key on the keyboard

key.description: Name of the key to press or a character to generate, such as `ArrowLeft` or `a`

browser_drag.name: browser_drag
browser_drag.description: Fallback only: use for a step that failed in two browser_run_code scripts or hit policy_denied. Perform drag and drop between two elements

startElement.description: Short plain-language name of the source element, shown to the user in review

startTarget.description: Source ref from the latest snapshot or browser_find (never text= or :has-text())

endElement.description: Short plain-language name of the destination element, shown to the user in review

endTarget.description: Destination ref from the latest snapshot or browser_find (never text= or :has-text())

browser_tabs.name: browser_tabs
browser_tabs.description: Fallback only: use for a step that failed in two browser_run_code scripts or hit policy_denied. List, create, close, or select a browser tab. new opens the tab and makes it current.

index.description: Tab index, used for close/select. If omitted for close, current tab is closed.

url.description: URL to navigate to in the new tab, used for new.

browser_take_screenshot.name: browser_take_screenshot
browser_take_screenshot.description: Take a screenshot of the current page. You can't perform actions based on the screenshot, use browser_snapshot for actions. The image comes back attached to this result.

element.description: Short plain-language name of the element, shown to the user in review

target.description: The ref from the latest snapshot or browser_find (never text= or :has-text())

fullPage.description: When true, takes a screenshot of the full scrollable page, instead of the currently visible viewport. Cannot be used with element screenshots.

Computer.name: Computer
Computer.description: Control your isolated box's desktop by screenshot, click, move, drag, type, key, scroll, and wait. Display is 1280×800. Computer click/move/scroll x,y are pixels in that space (origin top-left); never emit coordinates outside 0..1279 × 0..799. Use drag for scrollbars, sliders, moving windows, drag-selecting content, and revealing or repositioning offscreen UI. Shell runs in the same box: Shell for commands and files, Computer for the screen. Every call returns a screenshot of the resulting screen saved to disk; include that file:// path in your report to the parent when it should be shown to the user. When you already know the next few steps without needing to see the screen between them, such as typing into a field you just clicked, scrolling several times to read further down, or pressing Tab through a form, put them in then so they run in one call; that is several times faster than one call per action.

action.description: What to do on the box desktop. Every call captures a fresh screenshot of the resulting screen once all of its actions have run.

x.description: X pixel in the box display space (origin top-left) for click/move/scroll, or the start point for drag (omit to act at the cursor for click/move/scroll).

y.description: Y pixel in the box display space (origin top-left) for click/move/scroll, or the start point for drag (omit to act at the cursor for click/move/scroll).

x2.description: X pixel for the drag end point. Required with y2 when path is omitted.

y2.description: Y pixel for the drag end point. Required with x2 when path is omitted.

x.description: X pixel for this drag path point.

y.description: Y pixel for this drag path point.

path.description: Optional ordered drag path. A path with at least two {x, y} points is used verbatim instead of x/y/x2/y2.

text.description: Text to type. Required for type.

key.description: Key or chord in xdotool form, e.g. Return, ctrl+a, Alt+Left. Required for key. A shortcut meant to open a palette or search may not register. Check the returned screenshot that it opened and holds focus before typing a query into it.

button.description: Mouse button for click or drag (default left).

count.description: Click count for click: 1 single, 2 double, 3 triple.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held for the whole click, drag, or scroll, e.g. shift, ctrl, meta, ctrl+shift. Use for Shift-click range select and Ctrl/Cmd-click multi-select.

durationMs.description: Milliseconds to wait. Required for wait. Max 30000. A settle delay before the screenshot is automatic, so do not add a wait just to let the screen settle.

holdDurationMs.description: Milliseconds to keep the mouse button pressed before releasing it. Only valid for click. Use for press-and-hold "I'm human" widgets, holding until the widget completes; when it asks you to try again, hold longer. Max 30000. Cannot be combined with count > 1 or modifiers.

then.description: Up to 9 more actions to run in this same call, in order, right after the primary action. Each entry takes the same fields as the primary action. The whole sequence shares one 2000ms settle and returns one screenshot of the final screen, so batching is several times faster than a call per action. Batch only steps you already know without seeing the screen between them; when a step depends on what the previous one rendered, make separate calls. Allowed here: click, move, drag, type, key, scroll, wait.

description.description: Concise model-facing intent for this action. Include when it clarifies the action.

inputSchema.description: A computer-use action against the box desktop, optionally followed by more actions in the same call.

WakeParent.name: WakeParent
WakeParent.description: End this automation turn immediately and wake the parent agent so it can take over. You MUST use this when the saved instruction itself requires user-visible communication, such as pinging, reminding, telling, notifying, asking, or saying something to the user, because the parent is the only route to the user; a normal final assistant response does not wake the parent or reach the user. Old saved instructions may name SendMessage or SendToUser; both are deprecated and unavailable here, so treat either as communication intent, do not try to discover or call it, and use WakeParent with the complete payload or handoff. Also use this when the parent must communicate with another agent, make a decision, or handle a blocker you cannot resolve autonomously. Do not use it for background results that can wait until the parent's next natural safe boundary. Put the complete outcome, relevant context, and what the parent should communicate or do in the message; you cannot continue or add anything after this call.

message.description: The complete handoff for the parent: what happened, why it is being woken, and exactly what it should communicate or do next.

browser_run_code.name: browser_run_code
browser_run_code.description:
Automate a web task in one call: pass one async Playwright function, `async (page) => { ...; return value; }`, that does the task and returns what it found or did. Use it for every action in a web page, going to a URL included. Several items take one call that loops over them and returns an array, such as `async (page) => { const done = []; for (const row of await page.getByRole('row').all()) { await row.getByRole('checkbox').check(); done.push(await row.innerText()); } return done; }`, or a loop that calls page.goto for each URL you read. Send one call at a time and put dependent steps in one script: parallel calls on a page run one after another, and the later ones often find the page changed. await page.ariaSnapshot({ mode: 'ai' }) returns the page's accessibility tree with refs, as browser_snapshot does. A ref from either works as page.locator('aria-ref=<ref>'), such as await page.locator('aria-ref=e12').click(), in this call and later ones until the page navigates or re-renders that element. Pass { mode: 'ai' }: a snapshot without it has no refs. The return value is JSON-serialized into the result as `{"result": ..., "stdio": [...]}`, with console output in stdio. Return a short receipt such as `{ ok, url, summary }`, optionally with a `steps` array of what the script did. To see the page, return image Blobs directly or as top-level values, such as `{ after: new Blob([await page.screenshot()], { type: 'image/png' }) }`: each comes back as an image named by its key, at most 4 per call. A top-level `new Blob([await page.pdf()], { type: 'application/pdf' })` is saved under /workspace/browser-pdfs, and the result names its path, page count and size, so read it with your file tools. A page is always available: the selected tab, which is the one browser_snapshot reads, brought to the front first if it is hidden, or a new about:blank tab when none is open, so start with page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' }) when you need a site. To use another open tab, find it in page.context().pages() by its url() and call bringToFront() on it before click or hover, which wait for the tab to be in front; fill, press, reads and click({ force: true }) also work on a background tab. The tab a script leaves in front becomes the selected tab for the next call and browser_snapshot. Each call starts fresh with only page, console, Blob, Buffer, URL, TextEncoder and TextDecoder in scope, so there is no require, process, fetch or setTimeout. There is no expect; check conditions in code and return what you found. A call may run 30 seconds and return 256 KB. Actions time out after 5 s unless you pass timeout. Don't sleep with page.waitForTimeout; wait for the element, text or URL you expect. Every call on a locator is a round trip to the browser, so read a list or table with one allInnerTexts() or innerText() on its container.

Target what you have seen: click, fill and select through getByRole(role, { name, exact: true }) or getByLabel when browser_snapshot or browser_find showed that role, name or label, and otherwise through getByText(text, { exact: true }) on the exact text you read, scoped to its container, since text from innerText or textContent is not an accessible name. Never use a text= or :has-text() selector or CSS you haven't seen. When a locator matches several elements, scope it to the container you saw instead of taking .first(), which may be a hidden copy.

Blocked: in-page JavaScript (page.evaluate, evaluateHandle, $eval, $$eval, locator.evaluate, evaluateAll, waitForFunction, addScriptTag, setContent), so use the calls listed below instead; element handles (page.$, page.$$, elementHandle, elementHandles), so use locators; setViewportSize, response bodies, cookie and storage writes, request interception, direct HTTP requests (page.request, context.request), so open the URL with page.goto and read the page instead, file paths (screenshot or pdf path, tracing), new browsers or contexts, and URLs other than http, https and about:blank. To upload a file, call setInputFiles on the file input, even a hidden one, with an absolute path under /workspace or an in-memory { name, mimeType, buffer }. A file chooser an earlier call opened arrives as the second argument, async (page, { fileChooser }) => fileChooser.setFiles(path), and is null when none is open. Downloads save to /home/box/Downloads under Chrome's name. In a script, `const [d] = await Promise.all([page.waitForEvent('download'), page.click(…)])`, then `await d.path()` gives the saved file (d.failure() says why it failed); saveAs is blocked, so read the file with Read or Shell. goBack and goForward can hang waiting for load, so pass { waitUntil: "commit" }.

Instead of in-page JavaScript:
- Links or other attributes: for (const a of await page.locator('a').all()) out.push([await a.innerText(), await a.getAttribute('href')]).
- Form fields: await page.ariaSnapshot({ mode: 'ai' }) gives each field's role, name and value; inputValue() reads one.
- An element's role and name: await el.ariaSnapshot({ mode: 'ai' }); its markup: await el.locator('xpath=..').innerHTML(), or page.content() for the whole page.
- Set a value or click: fill(value), click({ force: true }).
- Scroll: el.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded(), or hover the list and page.mouse.wheel(0, 2000).

Failures return `{"error": {"code", "message"}, "stdio": [...]}`. policy_denied names the blocked API; do it another way. job_failed is an exception from your code, such as a TimeoutError from a missing element; fix the code. worker_failed is a browser or worker fault; retry once. timed_out means the call ran past 30 seconds; split it. The steps before a failure already ran, so continue from the failed step instead of rerunning the script.

code.description: A JavaScript function containing Playwright code to execute. It will be invoked with a single argument, page, which you can use for any page interaction. For example: `async (page) => { await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click(); return await page.title(); }`

browser_handle_dialog.name: browser_handle_dialog
browser_handle_dialog.description: Fallback only: use for a step that failed in two browser_run_code scripts or hit policy_denied. Handle a dialog

promptText.description: The text of the prompt in case of a prompt dialog.

browser_navigate_back.name: browser_navigate_back
browser_navigate_back.description: Fallback only: use for a step that failed in two browser_run_code scripts or hit policy_denied. Go back to the previous page in the history

level.description: Level of the console messages to return. Each level includes the messages of more severe levels. Defaults to "info".

all.description: Return all console messages since the beginning of the session, not just since the last navigation. Defaults to false.

browser_file_upload.name: browser_file_upload
browser_file_upload.description: Upload one or multiple files. Click the page's upload control first; this answers the file chooser it opens. Paths must be under /workspace.

paths.description: The absolute paths to the files to upload. Can be single file or multiple files. If omitted, file chooser is cancelled.

browser_find.name: browser_find
browser_find.description: Search the accessibility snapshot of the current page for text or a regular expression. Returns matching snapshot nodes with a few lines of surrounding context (like search snippets), each shown under its path from the root of the tree, which is cheaper than capturing the whole snapshot when you only need to locate an element and its ref.

text.description: Plain text to search for in the page snapshot (case-insensitive substring match). Provide either text or regex, not both.

regex.description: Regular expression to search for in the page snapshot. Matching is case-sensitive by default; wrap the pattern in slashes to add flags, e.g. "/error/i" for case-insensitive. Provide either text or regex, not both.

browser_fill_form.name: browser_fill_form
browser_fill_form.description: Fallback only: use for a step that failed in two browser_run_code scripts or hit policy_denied. Fill multiple form fields

element.description: Short plain-language name of the element, shown to the user in review

target.description: The ref from the latest snapshot or browser_find (never text= or :has-text())

value.description: Value to fill in the field. If the field is a checkbox, the value should be `true` or `false`. If the field is a combobox, the value should be the text of the option.

browser_hover.name: browser_hover
browser_hover.description: Fallback only: use for a step that failed in two browser_run_code scripts or hit policy_denied. Hover over element on page

element.description: Short plain-language name of the element, shown to the user in review

target.description: The ref from the latest snapshot or browser_find (never text= or :has-text())

browser_wait_for.name: browser_wait_for
browser_wait_for.description: Fallback only: use for a step that failed in two browser_run_code scripts or hit policy_denied. Wait for text to appear or disappear, or for a time. Actions already wait for the page to settle, so don't call this after a navigate, click, type or fill. Prefer text or textGone over a bare time.

time.description: Seconds to wait, at most 10. With text, the call returns once the text appears, and fails if it has not appeared within time or 10 s, whichever is longer. With textGone, it returns once the page has gone quiet and the text is gone, or after time if the text never shows. Without text or textGone, the wait returns as soon as the page has finished loading and gone quiet, so a long time costs no more on a quiet page.

textGone.description: The text to wait for to disappear

ReadTranscript.name: ReadTranscript
ReadTranscript.description: Read a full transcript: every user message, your replies, your reasoning, and each tool call with its input and result, one JSON object per line, oldest first. With no in it reads this conversation, including what was compacted out of your context, so use it to explain what you did in an earlier turn or routine run. Pass in=<id> for a Task subagent you dispatched, another agent the same user owns, or another of your conversations. Returns the newest messages first; page back with `before`.

in.description: Which transcript to read: "this" (the default) for this conversation, or the id of another of your conversations (a session_id from the other active conversations list), of another agent the same user owns (from your agent directory), or of a background subagent you dispatched with Task (the Agent ID from its result).

limit.description: How many of the newest messages to return (default 30, max 200).

before.description: Page back: return messages that come before this position. Use the `before` value from the previous result.

ReadAgentActivity.name: ReadAgentActivity
ReadAgentActivity.description: Read a bounded summary of what this user's other bots have been doing recently: per bot, when the user and the bot last spoke, its open todos, questions it asked the user that got no reply, and a short excerpt of the recent conversation, newest last. It sees only bots this user owns (team-shared and group bots are out of scope), only each bot's main conversation (never DM or Slack threads), and never this bot itself. It is read-only: nothing on the other bots is marked seen, answered, or touched. Use it to decide whether anything across the user's bots is worth raising.

since_hours.description: Only bots with a user or assistant message in the last N hours (default 72, capped at 168).

max_agents.description: Most bots to summarize, most recently active first (default 10, capped at 20).

excerpt_chars.description: Most characters of conversation excerpt per bot (default 1500, capped at 4000).
